coordinates.locator: OSM building footprint centroid for the Neutrino Monitor Building (tagged "Contains T2K ND280 Detectors"); the T2K NIM paper places ND280 280 m from the target in this building's pit
coordinates.note: Correction: replaces the campus-wide geocoder point (1.09 km away) with the surface building over the ND280/INGRID pit; a surface proxy for the underground pit, not a survey of the pit itself. Previous record: detector point 36.4587536, 140.599175 at 1500 m precision, sources ['src:t2k-nim-2011']; moved 859 m (2026-09-21).

depth.note: Depth of the near detector pit below the J-PARC surface, not a rock overburden for cosmic-ray shielding.
depth.quote: pit has a diameter of 17.5 m and a depth of 37 m, and has three floors.

name: J-PARC neutrino near detector hall (280 m)
notes: No published latitude/longitude for the near detector hall was found in any source read on 2026-09-16. The coordinates are the J-PARC site geocoder point; the hall is 280 m from the production target, i.e. well inside the precision quoted. Treat the position as site-scale, not survey-grade.
The T2K instrumentation paper gives the pit as 17.5 m diameter and 37 m deep; the KEK/J-PARC neutrino group page gives "a diameter of 17.5 m and a depth of 33.5 m".

summary.plain: An underground pit on the J-PARC site, 280 metres from the target where the neutrinos are made. It holds the detectors that measure the beam before the neutrinos have had time to change type.
summary.technical: Vertical pit 17.5 m in diameter and 37 m deep, 280 m downstream of the T2K production target, housing the on-axis INGRID modules and the off-axis ND280 detector at 2.5 degrees.
